**Section B: Vocabulary (10 marks).**

**I. Read this fax from James Steel and complete the sentences with appropriate words chosen from those in the brackets. (7 marks)**

Dear Mr Owen, I'm (1) .............. (attaching/enclosing/joining) a number of designs for you to consider for your stand at the international Food Exhibition next March. (For/So/As/like) (2) .............. you will see, there are a number of decisions you will have to make (before/prior/until) (3) .............. we can offer you an exact quotation. You should let us know: exactly how much floor space your stand will (employ/occupy/take) (4) .............. ; whether you require the stand to be open or closed; how many shelves you would like for displaying products; how many people you wish to accommodate on the stand at any one time, (involving/including/combining) (5) .............. both sales personnel and visitors. (Unless/Please/If) (6) .............. you would be so kind as to supply us with this information, we will send you a draft design (7) .............. (together/joined/also).
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Cette lettre commerciale (fax) teste des expressions figées propres à la correspondance professionnelle anglaise : "enclosing" pour une pièce jointe, "As you will see" en tête de paragraphe, des connecteurs de condition et de temps, et le vocabulaire technique de l'aménagement d'un stand d'exposition.

1. **enclosing.** Dans une lettre commerciale, "I am enclosing..." est la formule consacrée pour annoncer une pièce jointe.

(Unless/Please/If) (6) .............. you would be so kind as to supply us with this information, we will send you a draft design (7) .............. (together/joined/also).
questions.corrige_markdown:
7. **also.** "We will send you a draft design also" indique un envoi supplémentaire, en complément de ce qui a déjà été annoncé.

### Piège à éviter
"Unless" introduirait une condition négative contraire au sens attendu (une requête polie, non une menace conditionnelle) : vérifie toujours que le connecteur choisi correspond au ton du message, ici poli et commercial.

### Conseil
Dans les lettres professionnelles anglaises, apprends les formules figées comme des blocs entiers ("I am enclosing", "As you will see", "would be so kind as to") plutôt que mot par mot : cela permet de les reconnaître immédiatement dans un nouveau contexte.

**Section B: Vocabulary (10 marks).**

**II. Transform each sentence below using the expressions in the brackets. Each sentence has been started for you. (3 marks)**
1. Do you and your twin brother have the same looks? (to resemble)
Does ......................................................... ?
questions.corrige_markdown: 1. **Does your twin brother resemble you?** "Resemble" (ressembler à) remplace "have the same looks as", en gardant le sens de la question fermée d'origine.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section B: Vocabulary (10 marks).**

**II. Transform each sentence below using the expressions in the brackets. Each sentence has been started for you. (3 marks)**
2. I'd rather have a block of ice and a bottle of coke than a bottle of beer. (prefer)
I .........................................................
questions.corrige_markdown: 2. **I prefer a block of ice and a bottle of coke to a bottle of beer.** "Prefer X to Y" est la structure figée équivalente à "would rather have X than Y".

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section B: Vocabulary (10 marks).**

**II. Transform each sentence below using the expressions in the brackets. Each sentence has been started for you. (3 marks)**
3. The Senior Discipline Master is interviewing the students who stole books from the school library. (interviewed)
The students ......................................................... by the Senior Discipline Master.
questions.corrige_markdown:
3. **The students who stole books from the school library are being interviewed by the Senior Discipline Master.** Le présent continu actif ("is interviewing") se transforme au passif continu correspondant : "are being interviewed".

### Piège à éviter
Dans la transformation "prefer X to Y", n'utilise jamais "than" après "prefer" ("prefer X than Y" est incorrect) : seul "rather...than" accepte "than", tandis que "prefer" exige "to".

### Conseil
Pour repérer le bon temps du passif, identifie d'abord précisément le temps de la phrase active de départ (ici le présent continu "is interviewing") : le passif doit conserver exactement ce même temps sous la forme "be + being + participe passé".
